2027-03-22.title: Hasha Monday · Monday of Passion Week
readings: The Lord a garland of glory; “This is rest; give rest to the weary”

2027-03-22.alt: Hasha Week, the week of the Lord's Passion (Kashtanubhava Azhcha), which began on the evening of Hosanna Sunday. The Panchangam notes that the newly prepared Hasha Week lectionary gives an Old Testament reading, an Epistle and a Gospel for every hour of prayer this week; the readings below are the ones the Panchangam lists for the day. The Panchangam also remembers Rev. Fr Seraphion Attupurathu OIC (Alexander Shemmashan), who came into Catholic communion in the reunion of 1930 and died in 1975.
2027-03-22.verse: But you are the same, and your years will never end.
theo: Last evening, as Hosanna Sunday closed, our Church entered Hasha Week. Hasho is the Syriac word for suffering: this is the week of the Lord's Passion, and the Church walks beside him day by day. On Monday the Gospel finds Jesus in the temple at Jerusalem, teaching, a few days before his death. The chief priests and the elders come with a question: “By what authority are you doing these things, and who gave you this authority?” Jesus answers with a question of his own: “Did the baptism of John come from heaven, or was it of human origin?” They weigh the answer by what it will cost them, not by what is true, and at last say: “We do not know.” St John Chrysostom notes that the Lord did not refuse to answer people who wished to learn, but people who asked only in order to trap him (in substance). The question is not only theirs. Each of us knows how to say “We do not know” when the truth would ask too much. This week Jesus will answer the question of his authority, not with argument, but with the Cross and the empty tomb.

Isaiah shows why some do not hear. God offers himself as “a garland of glory, and a diadem of beauty, to the remnant of his people,” but the leaders of the city are drunk: “the priest and the prophet reel with strong drink.” They mock the prophet's plain teaching as baby talk, “precept upon precept... line upon line, here a little, there a little.” Yet the message God sent was simple and kind: “This is rest; give rest to the weary; and this is repose”; “yet they would not hear.” The Letter to the Hebrews then lifts our eyes to who it is that stands in the temple. To the Son the Father says: “In the beginning, Lord, you founded the earth, and the heavens are the work of your hands; they will perish, but you remain.” Everything wears out like clothing, “But you are the same, and your years will never end.” The man questioned in the temple courts is the Lord who laid the foundations of the earth. He has every authority, and he uses it this week to lay down his life for us.

How does a family keep Hasha Week? First, by going with the Church to the prayers of the hours. This week our Church prays the Evening, Compline, Night, Morning, Third, Sixth and Ninth Hours with special solemnity, and the new Hasha Week lectionary gives readings from the Old Testament, the Apostle and the Gospel for each hour; follow your parish timetable for the hours and for the Holy Qurbono. Second, by keeping the fast and the abstinence of the Great Lent to its end, with the prostrations (kumbideel) as your parish practises them; the Panchangam asks priests to remind the faithful of the special prayers and abstinences of this week. Third, by preparing for Pesaha with a good confession before Thursday. At home, light the lamp in the evening, read the day's Gospel aloud, pray the evening prayer from the Shehimo, and end with a few moments of silence before the cross. Today we also remember Fr Seraphion Attupurathu OIC, known as Alexander Shemmashan, who came into Catholic communion in the reunion of 1930 and served the Church until his death in 1975.
outline: Ask: when have I said “I do not know” because the truth would cost me?
The question in the temple and the answer of the Cross.
God's simple word, and the hearts that would not hear.
The Lord who founded the earth goes to his Passion.
“But you are the same, and your years will never end.”
live: This Hasha Week, take one burden off someone tired: a chore, an errand, a visit, a meal.
Name one truth you have been avoiding with “I do not know,” and bring it to confession before Pesaha.
2027-03-22.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, in the beginning you founded the earth, and the heavens are the work of your hands; you remain when all things wear out. In these holy days you walked into Jerusalem to suffer for us. Give us hearts that hear your word and do not evade it. Make us a people who give rest to the weary. Keep us close to you through this week of your Passion, that we may rejoice in your Resurrection. Grant eternal rest to Fr Seraphion and to all who have served your Church faithfully. Amen.
altar: The Son who will never change offers himself in the Holy Qurbono as the true rest of the weary, the living bread that does not wear out.

quick: God offered his people rest, but their leaders would not hear.
The heavens wear out like clothing; the Lord remains the same.
In the temple Jesus was asked: by what authority? His answer would be the Cross.
2027-03-22.action: Do one hidden act of service today for someone who is tired.
2027-03-22.question: Where do I say “I do not know” to avoid what God is asking?

family.explain: This week is Hasha Week, the week when Jesus suffered and died for us. In the temple some leaders asked Jesus who gave him the right to do what he did. Jesus knew they were not really looking for the truth. Jesus is God's Son; everything belongs to him. This week he will show his power by loving us all the way to the Cross.
family.intention: We pray that our family will keep this holy week with Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “What can our family do each evening this week to stay close to Jesus?”

illus: In a parish near Mavelikara the sacristan, an old man, used to put the same faded purple cloth on the lectern every Hasha Week. One year the youth group bought a new one and asked him to throw the old cloth away. He held it up to the light. It was thin, mended in three places. He said: this cloth has worn out serving the word. The word has not worn out at all. Put the new one on, but let me keep this one. They let him keep it, and on Good Friday he knelt on it at the back of the church.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, in this week of your Passion we come to stay with you. Open our ears to your word. Amen.
share: This is rest; give rest to the weary... yet they would not hear (Isaiah 28:12). Where have I refused to hear God?
They will perish, but you remain (Hebrews 1:11). What in my life is wearing out, and what remains?
By what authority are you doing these things? (Matthew 21:23). Do I let Jesus have authority over my week?
interc: For our Church as it enters Hasha Week, that we may keep these days with prayer and fasting.
For all who will come to confession this week, and for the priests who will hear them.
For people who are worn out by work, illness or grief, that someone may give them rest.
For leaders in Church and society, that they may seek truth and not their own safety.
For the soul of Fr Seraphion Attupurathu and for all who came into Catholic communion in the reunion of 1930.
pm.close: Father, your Son did not answer with force but with the gift of his life. Keep us beside him through this week, give rest to the weary through our hands, and bring us with joy to the day of his Resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, last evening Hasha Week began, the week of our Lord's Passion. Today the Gospel shows Jesus in the temple, and the chief priests and elders ask him: by what authority are you doing these things, and who gave you this authority? (Matthew 21:23).

Jesus asks them about John's baptism, and they answer: we do not know (Matthew 21:27). They knew, but the truth would cost them. Let us be honest: we too say “I do not know” when God asks something hard of us.

Isaiah tells of a people to whom God said: this is rest; give rest to the weary; yet they would not hear (Isaiah 28:12). And Hebrews sings to the Son: they will perish, but you remain (Hebrews 1:11). The Lord who made heaven and earth stands in the temple and lets himself be questioned.

His answer will come on Friday: not a speech, but the Cross; and on Sunday, the empty tomb. This week let us go to the prayers of the hours, keep the fast, make a good confession, and give rest to someone who is weary. Amen.
kids: Children, this week is called Hasha Week. It is the most special week of the year, because Jesus suffered and died for us, and then rose again. Some people asked Jesus: who gave you the power to do these things? Jesus is God's Son. All power belongs to him, and he used it to love us. Can you say a short prayer to Jesus every evening this week?

intro: Theme: “But you are the same, and your years will never end.”
On Hasha Monday: the question in the temple, the rest God offers, and the Lord who remains.

q: To him was given dominion and glory and kingship, that all peoples, nations, and languages should serve him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion that shall not pass away, and his kingship is one that shall never be destroyed.
No one takes it from me, but I lay it down of my own accord. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it up again. I have received this command from my Father.
points.apply: Bring one truth you have been avoiding to confession before Pesaha.

sub: A garland of glory for the remnant.
q: Thus says the Lord: Stand at the crossroads, and look, and ask for the ancient paths, where the good way lies; and walk in it, and find rest for your souls.
Come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest.
points.apply: Take one burden off a weary person during Hasha Week.

sub: The heavens wear out like clothing.
The Son who founded the earth.
He goes freely to his Passion.
q: but you are the same, and your years have no end.
I was dead, and see, I am alive forever and ever; and I have the keys of Death and of Hades.
points.apply: Each evening this week, end the day with a few minutes of silence before the cross.

concl: The Lord of all lets himself be questioned, and answers with his life.
Hasha Week asks us to stop evading and to stay with him.
2027-03-22.resolve: Keep the hours, the fast and a good confession this Hasha Week, and give rest to someone who is weary.
